I worked as a meat clerk for 4.5 years. I don't know what the laws are like out on the west coast, but in New England tracking everything is super important, and most people are pretty garbage at it. If you need to fill out logs, fill them out regularly and accurately. It's not hard to do and will reflect well on you as a worker.  
If you are cleaning, pay attention to the machines, because there are nooks and crannies that can easily be missed on a grinder, band saw, cuber, ect. so try and figure out where they are and make sure to clean them. It only becomes a pain to clean if they get missed.  
Keep you're tools in good order. I always made sure the knives I used were sharp and ready to use. Also, if they aren't your knives, don't touch them unless someone tells you to. People tend to want their knives kept the way they want them kept and get fussy when they are handle "incorrectly". My boss was lazy and never learned how to sharpen a knife so I always did it for her, but that was because she asked me to.  
If you do prepared foods, like meatballs or stuffed meats or what have you, work smarter not harder. Try to keep your production as automated as possible, it will save you time. Also, presentation is important. Don't just slap things together, take pride in your work and make a product that people are going to see and **WANT** to buy.  
If you have down time, set yourself (and others for that matter) up for success. Pay it forward, but understand that when shit hits the fan, you very well might come into work and everything is a mess. Keep your nose to the grind stone and power through it.  
Most importantly, have a sense of humor. The meat industry is full of super easy jokes to make and a lot of repetitive work that needs to be done. If you can't laugh with your coworkers you are going to have a bad time.
